original_test_intent: Stress system hard-reset and BMC management recovery for 500 IPMI OOB resets while observing console behavior and ensuring final BMC functionality and clean diagnostics.
original_method: On a dedicated recoverable SUT, issue one supported hard reset at a time, wait for bounded BMC/IPMI/LAN/host recovery, record SOL/KVM disconnect and reconnection under an approved policy, preserve diagnostic deltas and stop on the first unsafe anomaly.
manual_activity: Approve the target, IPMI channel/cipher and hard-reset semantics, 500-cycle cadence, BMC/host recovery deadlines, retry/abort thresholds and whether SOL/KVM acceptance means persistence or reconnection; assign an operator for console evidence.
required_inputs: Stable power and independent OOB recovery
Pinned reviewed script revision or equivalent approved procedure
safety_requirements: Issue one reset only after prior-cycle recovery is verified
Stop on identity drift, recovery timeout, unexpected diagnostics or lost OOB path
Do not alter BIOS, boot, network or firewall settings
agent_execution_scope: Measure SOL/KVM disconnect/reconnect under approved semantics
Repeat only after a complete cycle

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The reset operation and count match the source, but hardcoded cipher 17 is not validated, command-line passwords are unsafe, and a loop without recovery polling and stop gates can issue a reset before the prior boot completes.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved IPMI hard-reset command with secret-backed credentials once per cycle, then block on verified BMC/IPMI/LAN/host recovery and console evidence before any next reset.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The hard-reset action, 500 count and 20/1440 timing fields remain; interval, cipher/channel, deadlines and session semantics are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Represent each reset as an auditable state machine: request accepted, host power transition, BMC continuity, host boot, management recovery, console observation and diagnostic delta.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes plaintext credentials and blind looping, adds one-cycle rehearsal, bounded recovery, operator evidence, per-cycle logs and abort/recovery controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates the approved OOB hard-reset path on one target; it does not test graceful reboot, full AC removal, BMC reset, alternate IPMI channels or workload crash consistency beyond the supplied checks.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Hard resets can corrupt active data and a late-recovering host can be reset again by an unsafe timer. BMC may remain reachable while host boot or console recovery fails.

project_override_considerations: Procedure names KVM while Criteria requires SOL; retain separate evidence for both if both are mandatory. A session may disconnect during host reset, so 'always connected' needs an approved persistence/reconnect definition rather than a literal unsupported assertion.
expected_evidence: Approval, dedicated target and recovery readiness
Final completed count and system state
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure says keep KVM connected while Criteria requires SOL always connected, and a host hard reset normally interrupts host console output. The review preserves both named interfaces and requires an approved persistence-versus-reconnect acceptance contract without altering Master.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The reset method, recovery deadlines, console semantics and abort controls are identifiable package/approval inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Converts a credential-leaking blind reset loop into a per-cycle recoverability test and exposes the SOL/KVM continuity ambiguity instead of claiming an impossible uninterrupted session.
independent_technical_reasoning: `chassis power reset` forces a host reset but normally leaves the BMC running, so BMC reachability and host/SOL/KVM continuity are different observables. The next reset must not be issued until host boot and management recovery are proven, otherwise cycle count loses meaning and damage compounds. A console disconnect can be expected while permanent loss or late reconnection is a defect only under a specified window. Per-cycle SEL and OS evidence is necessary because final logs cannot reliably attribute transient reset failures.
